name: Ketamine
route_note: IV or IM injection for anaesthesia and procedural sedation; subanaesthetic infusions used in pain and depression settings.
owner: generic (many); Par Pharmaceutical (Ketalar, US), Pfizer (Ketalar, some markets)

discovery.note: Developed as a shorter-acting, less hallucinogenic alternative to phencyclidine (PCP); first human studies by Edward Domino and Guenter Corssen in 1964.

tagline: Dissociative anaesthetic that preserves breathing, now also a rapid antidepressant
summary: Ketamine is a dissociative anaesthetic that blocks NMDA receptors. Because it maintains airway reflexes, breathing and blood pressure, it is widely used in emergency, battlefield and low-resource anaesthesia. Since the 2000s, subanaesthetic doses have been studied for rapid relief of depression, leading to the development of esketamine. It is also used recreationally and is a controlled substance.
mechanism: Ketamine is a non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist that binds within the open ion channel (the PCP site). Disrupted thalamocortical and limbic signalling produces a 'dissociative' state of analgesia, amnesia and unconsciousness with preserved reflexes.

It stimulates the sympathetic nervous system, generally raising heart rate and blood pressure and causing bronchodilation. Its antidepressant effects are thought to involve a glutamate surge, AMPA receptor activation, BDNF release and synaptogenesis; analgesic effects relate to reduced central sensitisation.
uses: Induction and maintenance of general anaesthesia
Procedural sedation and analgesia (including in children)
Anaesthesia in haemodynamically unstable or asthmatic patients
Off-label: acute and chronic pain, treatment-resistant depression

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Calvin Stevens synthesises CI-581 at Parke-Davis.

history.title: First human use
history.detail: Domino and Corssen test ketamine in prisoner volunteers and coin the term 'dissociative anaesthesia'.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Ketalar is approved in the US; it is used widely by US forces in the Vietnam War.

history.title: Scheduling
history.detail: Ketamine is placed in US Schedule III.

history.title: Antidepressant signal
history.detail: Berman and colleagues report rapid antidepressant effects of a single subanaesthetic infusion.

history.title: NIMH trial
history.detail: Zarate and colleagues confirm rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression.

history.title: Esketamine
history.detail: The S-enantiomer is approved as Spravato nasal spray for treatment-resistant depression.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 to active norketamine

serious: Respiratory depression with rapid injection or other depressants

facts: Ketamine's preservation of breathing makes it a key anaesthetic where ventilators are scarce.
Chronic recreational use can cause severe ulcerative cystitis.
